source_title: Inside Patrick Stewart and Wife Sunny Ozell’s Love Story, from Their Chance Meeting to His Final Days - People.com
source_excerpt:
Stewart and Ozell tied the knot in a 2013 ceremony officiated by Ian McKellen
The Star Trek and X-Men star married singer-songwriter Sunny Ozell in 2013
The two met in New York in 2008, as Stewart recalled to PEOPLE: “My life is perpetually interesting — and it’s largely as a result of Sunny,” he shared
Sir Patrick Stewart has died , leaving behind a legacy of acclaimed performances on stage and screen, as well as decades of activism. His wife, Sunny Ozell , whom he married in 2013, was by his side.
“We announce with great sorrow the passing of Sir Patrick Stewart yesterday at his home in Los Angeles, in the loving care of his beloved wife Sunny, following a brief and poignant journey with Alzheimer’s Disease and Lewy Body Dementia,” read a statement from a spokesperson on Thursday, Oct. 29.
Stewart and singer-songwriter Ozell, 47, first met in 2008 at Franny’s, a now-closed pizzeria in Brooklyn where she was working as a waitress at the time.
The Star Trek star recalled their meet-cute to PEOPLE in 2022, explaining that he was starring in William Shakespeare’s Macbeth on Broadway at the time.
“This lovely woman came over and said, ‘Gentleman, on the house, what would you like for desserts?’ We got talking and she told me how much she’d wanted to see Macbeth , but it had been sold out,” he recalled.
Stewart went on to give Ozell his phone number, recalling that it “was the only time in my life I’ve given someone my telephone number and said, ‘Call me.’” The pair later reconnected backstage after a performance of Macbeth and went on a date. “We had dinner and here we are,” he said.
“I’ve never met anyone like her before,” the actor told PEOPLE. “She is so smart and so informed. And her intellectual accomplishments are extraordinary. She remembers everything. My life is perpetually interesting — and it’s largely as a result of Sunny.”
After several years of dating, the couple tied the knot in September 2013 during a ceremony in Lake Tahoe officiated by Stewart’s longtime friend and X-Men costar Sir Ian McKellen . Ozell was born and raised in Reno, Nevada, not far from where the wedding took place.
Stewart marked the occasion with a playful social media post featuring the newlyweds smiling together in a ball pit. “Yes, married,” he captioned the photo.
Years later, Stewart revealed that McKellen had not been legally authorized to officiate weddings in Nevada, meaning the couple’s Lake Tahoe ceremony was not legally binding. During a 2020 appearance on Jimmy Kimmel Live! , Stewart told guest host Pete Buttigieg that he and Ozell “were formally married in a Mexican restaurant” in Los Angeles, with a handful of friends in attendance and McKellen officiating in a “kind of robe.”
“Our guests had no idea what was happening,” he recalled.
The Logan star was previously married to Sheila Falconer from 1966 to 1990 and Wendy Neuss from 2000 to 2003. Stewart shares a son and a daughter with Falconer.
Ozell made an appearance in a 2022 episode of the second season of her husband’s Paramount+ series Star Trek: Picard , performing with her band during a nightclub scene.
“I wasn’t called the day that Sunny and her band filmed the scene, but I couldn’t resist going to the set all the same to watch her work,” Stewart told TV Insider in July 2026. “I’ve always felt that her music is quite cinematic, and it was a brilliant fit for the episode itself.”
The couple frequently shared glimpses of their life together in Los Angeles on social media. In 2013, Ozell posted a sweet video of Stewart giving a “masterclass” on how to perform a “quadruple take,” which went viral.
In 2017, the Star Trek star also shared updates about a pit bull named Ginger whom the couple fostered through Los Angeles-based rescue organization Wags and Walks . Stewart also partnered with the ASPCA to advocate for an end to dogfighting.

In a statement, Stewart’s spokesperson said the actor “has been held in the warm embrace of family and friends, surrounded by live music, prayer, tears, laughter, and the kind of profound emotion that only he could inspire after a lifetime of devotion to us all.”
“We will forever cherish the peaceful ease and reflection on his face, an enduring reminder of his invincible grace,” the statement continued.
